findings.evidence: "In addition, eligibility for the workspace stipend depends on several details the reviewer checks one at a time. The workspace must sit inside the employee's primary residence for the stipend to apply. A workspace located in a shared coworking space does not qualify for the stipend under this section. A workspace used only occasionally for calls does not meet the bar the stipend policy sets. The reviewer confirms the workspace address matches the address already on file with payroll. A workspace shared with a roommate can still qualify if the desk area belongs to the employee alone. The stipend covers only the equipment placed inside that confirmed workspace, nothing located elsewhere in the home. A workspace that changes address during the benefit year needs a fresh confirmation before the stipend continues. The reviewer logs every workspace confirmation in the same shared tracking sheet the benefits team maintains. A workspace confirmation from more than one year ago no longer satisfies the stipend requirement on its own."
findings.fix: Reformat as a bulleted list with one requirement per bullet point.
findings.location: Eligibility section, paragraph starting "In addition, eligibility for the workspace stipend depends on several details"
findings.violation: This paragraph presents nine distinct eligibility requirements as a long narrative, making them difficult to identify and verify as a checklist.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category."
findings.fix: Break into multiple shorter sentences such as: "However, exceptions to the one-device limit may apply. The benefits team can approve a second device per category if the role genuinely requires it due to regular fieldwork. Secondary devices are tracked by the finance office against the same annual budget amount published in the equipment catalog."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, second sentence
findings.violation: This sentence is a run-on containing multiple nested clauses, making it difficult to parse the policy on multiple devices.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review. Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person: "Employees record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review. Employees submit requests in the portal and track status there until the payment clears."
findings.violation: This section shifts to second person ("you") while the rest of the document uses passive or third-person voice, creating inconsistent tone and perspective.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Expand to match How to Apply requirements: "Completing the request involves confirming eligibility, uploading the receipt, submitting the manager's approval form, and providing the original purchase order."
findings.violation: This description omits required items (manager's approval form and purchase order) that are specified in the How to Apply section, creating inconsistency.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison reviews the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Either retitle the section to "Budget Review Process" or replace with content describing actual exceptions to standard stipend policy.
findings.violation: The section titled "Special Cases" contains budget process information rather than actual special cases or policy exceptions.

findings.evidence: "The escalation of repeat requests happens automatically within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Clarify: "If an employee resubmits a request within the same benefit quarter, it will be automatically escalated to a supervisor for expedited review."
findings.violation: The term "repeat requests" is undefined - the document does not explain what qualifies as a repeat request or what escalation entails.

findings.evidence: "The people operations office tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Replace with unique content such as contact information for questions, procedures for policy updates, or links to support resources.
findings.violation: This content nearly duplicates information already presented in Program Overview, adding no new information.
